news.title: Did a suicide bomb plot target Messi and Ronaldo at 2026 World Cup?
news.lede: A leaked police dossier has revealed the extent of the security threats that surrounded the 2026 FIFA World Cup, including alleged terror plots and death threats targeting some of the tournament’s biggest stars and match officials.The United States co-hosted the tournament alongside Mexico and Canada, with Spain lifting the trophy after defeating Argentina 1-0 in the final.According to a report by The Sun, citing Spanish outlet Informacion.es, Argentina captain Lionel Messi was at the centre of several serious threats. Ahead of Argentina’s group-stage match against Jordan, a man allegedly called Dallas Airport and threatened to storm the stadium with two accomplices armed with hand grenades and a rifle. He vowed to attack police officers and players from both teams, while also issuing a death threat against Messi..

news.title: Infantino’s World Cup sell-off debacle has rocked football but Fifa’s crisis has deep and rotten roots
news.lede: It has been a remarkable few days for an institution that may be irredeemable but this is a story that stretches back to a decision in 2010. There are decades in which nothing happens, and weeks in which decades happen, and those weeks tend to result in leaders being toppled. Not even a fortnight ago, Gianni Infantino was taking his victory lap on Instagram, attacking “those behind their pens and papers, behind their screens spreading hate and false rumours” who had dared to question elements of his World Cup, which had generated a record $15bn in revenues. But the next day came the revelation of his plan to sell the World Cup to outside investors and a backlash that has him scrabbling to save his presidency.

news.title: 'A man of his word': Spain's Gavi finally reveals World Cup promise everyone was waiting for
news.lede: Spain midfielder Gavi has fulfilled one of the more memorable promises made during his country's victorious FIFA World Cup campaign, unveiling a striking new pink hairstyle after La Roja lifted the trophy in New York last month. The Barcelona star had vowed to dye his hair if Spain became world champions, and this week he followed through, joining a growing list of teammates who have honoured their own World Cup pledges." news.title: Gianni Infantino: Politicians, private jets and power - the life of a Fifa president
news.lede: Gianni Infantino, pictured with Colombian FA president Ramon Jesurun, is attending the inauguration of the country's new president Abelardo de la Espriella. Gianni Infantino stepped off a plane in Cali and was greeted on the runway by the president of the Colombian Football Federation. Ramon Jesurun, a close ally of Infantino's, saw it as a chance to show his support, with the two men smiling in a photo opportunity for the federation's Instagram account. Infantino had not travelled to Colombia for any run-of-the-mill meeting on Friday.

news.title: Vincent Kompany says Bayern Munich star Joshua Kimmich still dealing with lingering issue from World Cup
news.lede: Bayern Munich fans can breathe a little easier after Vincent Kompany provided an update on Joshua Kimmich’s fitness following the club’s 2-1 preseason win over Aston Villa. Although Kimmich did not feature in the friendly, Kompany revealed that the midfielder’s absence was purely a precaution as he continues to manage a lingering issue dating back to the World Cup. ”He has a little bit something he still carries from the World Cup. He trained this morning but wasn’t involved in the game.

news.title: World Cup winner showcases incredible physique aged 56 and gives fans achievable workout tip
news.lede: The ex-Bayern Munich star, now 56, won it all as a player. He scooped the Champions League, European Championship, World Cup and six Bundesliga titles, plus the Intercontinental Cup and individual awards from UEFA and FIFA. And the left-back did it in the era of Roberto Carlos too. Since retiring in 2006, Lizarazu hasn't taken his foot off the gas, rather he's put his foot to the floor.
